newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called slightly off tracking ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called slightly off tracking ACCESS.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called steady to slightly lower Friday, tracking ACCESS amid no news in what traders expected would be a lacklustre trading session with prices drifting about unchanged.
"The call is a unchanged to boring. There is no news. London is just a bit lower, but we seem to be drifting in a rangebound market," said a New York dealer.
Crude was called steady to five cents lower a barrel. Refined products were called steady to 0.25 cent a gallon lower.
At 0914 EDT, June Brent was off three cents a barrel at $19.46.
"The market seems to have gotten really comfortable in this range," said a New York crude dealer of spot crude's $20.50 to 21.50 range it entered after Monday's upside breakout.
But, technicians noted Monday's upside breakout gave rise to a bullish pennant formation on the June crude chart, formed by the week's sideways action.

"This kind of pattern usually means the uptrend will continue, and makes crude look more attractive in light of the gap below it which has not been filled," said High Yield Analytics analyst Tom Bentz.
Spot crude has a gap extending to the $20.50 area left since Monday.
On Thursday, June gasoline ended 0.34 cent a gallon lower at 64.04 cents. June crude finished nine cents a barrel lower at $21.30 while June heating oil ended 0.06 cent a gallon up at 56.48 cents.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
